misconception: Unquoted supplied values split spaces into extra arguments.

alternate:
if test -n "$1"; then
printf '%s%s\n' 'Destination: ' "$1"
else
printf '%s\n' 'Destination required' >&2
exit 2
fi

for item in "$@"; do
printf '%s%s\n' 'File: ' "$item"
cat "$item"
done
incorrect: for item in $@; do printf 'File: %s\n' "$item"; cat "$item"; done
misconception: Unquoted argument vector loses filename boundaries.

alternate:
if [ -n "$2" ] && [ -f "$1" ]; then
grep -F ERROR "$1" > "$2"
printf 'Saved: %s\n' "$2"
else
printf '%s\n' 'Cannot build report' >&2
exit 2
fi

misconception: Component-only selection also retains non-error entries.

alternate:
while read -r ticket || test -n "$ticket"; do
printf '%s%s\n' 'Ticket: ' "$ticket"
done
incorrect: while read -r line; do printf 'Ticket: %s\n' "$line"; done
misconception: Drops a nonempty last line without a final line break.

alternate:
problem=no
for item in "$@"; do
if test -f "$item"; then
printf '%s%s\n' 'File: ' "$item"
grep -F ERROR "$item"
else
printf '%s%s\n' 'Missing: ' "$item" >&2
problem=yes
fi
done
if test "$problem" = yes; then exit 2; fi
exit 0
incorrect:
for path in "$@"; do
if [ -f "$path" ]; then
printf 'File: %s\n' "$path"
grep -F ERROR "$path"
else
printf 'Missing: %s\n' "$path" >&2
exit 2
fi
done
exit 0
misconception: Stops on first missing file and skips later valid work.
